long.vo: India have won two Test series in New Zealand. In fifty-eight years. The last one was in two thousand and nine. Next week, a new-look India try again. Here's why it's so hard, and why this time might be different.

scene.kicker: INDIA IN NEW ZEALAND · TEST SERIES

long.vo: Start with the history. India's first ever overseas series win came here, in nineteen sixty-eight. Then nothing for forty-one years, until MS Dhoni's side won in two thousand and nine. Since then: beaten in twenty fourteen, and beaten two-nil on the last tour, in twenty twenty.

head.t: INDIA'S TEST SERIES IN NEW ZEALAND

long.vo: In twenty-six Tests in New Zealand, India have won just five. And it isn't only away from home. New Zealand beat India in the first World Test Championship final, and in twenty twenty-four, they did something no touring side had managed in twelve years. They beat India, in India. Three-nil.

tiles.l: LOST THE WTC FINAL TO NZ

long.vo: So why is New Zealand so hard? The answer is in who takes the wickets. Since twenty ten, eighty-six per cent of all wickets in Tests in New Zealand have gone to fast bowlers. In India, it's forty-three per cent. It's a different game.

head.sub: SHARE OF TEST WICKETS TAKEN BY PACE · 2010-2025

long.vo: And India's batters feel it. Since two thousand and nine, they've averaged thirty-five and a half runs per wicket in New Zealand, against nearly forty-one at home. The ball does more, for longer, and the wind at the Basin Reserve can make one end feel like a different pitch.

The New Zealand plan is simple. Full, swinging and seaming with the new ball, a packed slip cordon, and patience. At the Basin Reserve, the first-innings average since twenty ten is three hundred and thirty-nine. Batting first is no advantage: of twenty Tests, the side batting first won seven, the side batting second won eight.

But this is not the New Zealand that beat India last time. The three bowlers with the most Test wickets against India, Tim Southee, Trent Boult and Ajaz Patel, are not in this squad. Southee and Neil Wagner have retired, and Kane Williamson retired in June.

head.sub: NZ BOWLERS' TEST WICKETS AGAINST INDIA · 2003-2024

long.vo: The man India need to watch is Kyle Jamieson. At six foot eight, he gets bounce from a length that other bowlers can't. He has twenty-two Test wickets against India, and he was player of the match in that World Test Championship final.

scene.note: 6 ft 8 in: extra bounce from a good length

long.vo: Alongside him: Matt Henry, Jacob Duffy, Nathan Smith and Blair Tickner. With Mitchell Santner as the spinner. And don't write them off. New Zealand are third in the World Test Championship, and they won two-one in England this summer.

items.h: JACOB DUFFY · NATHAN SMITH · BLAIR TICKNER

long.vo: Now India. Only three of their sixteen players have ever played a Test in New Zealand: जसप्रीत बुमराह, रवींद्र जडेजा, and Rishabh Pant, who is still waiting on fitness.

scene.label: INDIA'S SQUAD WHO HAVE PLAYED A TEST IN NEW ZEALAND

long.vo: But the squad is built for these conditions. Five fast bowlers, led by बुमराह, who averages under twenty in fifty-two Tests. A young top order under captain शुभमन गिल. And कुलदीप यादव as the only specialist spinner.

items.d: Captain, leading a young top order

long.vo: The battle that decides the series? बुमराह against Tom Latham. The left-handed captain against the best fast bowler in the world, with a new ball, in New Zealand.
There's a lot riding on it. New Zealand sit third in the World Test Championship, India fifth. Two wins here, and India are right back in the race for next year's final.

head.sub: POINTS PERCENTAGE · 2025-27 CYCLE · BEFORE THE SERIES

long.vo: Our verdict? New Zealand at home are still favourites. But their attack has far less experience than the one India faced in twenty twenty, and India have the best bowler on either side. We're calling it one-all.

scene.sub: New Zealand are favourites at home. Bumrah is India's equaliser.
